title: Transport three-frame character exclusions across count profiles: (1,1,2,0) excluded, twelve profiles not character-excludable (no κ)
body:
## Result

No κ claim and no word. The selected record is unchanged.

In the PR2085/2112 register model with three added signed rank-one frames, eight linear symmetries of the address space permute the old labels `A, B, P, Q` and the four targets. They carry the whole character table of a decomposition of one old-count profile to its image. Three results follow for the census in discussion comment 19377345.

1. **`(1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1)` admits no seven-call word.** It is the image of `(2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1)` under the map `M -> W M W^T / 2`, `W = [[1,1],[1,-1]]`, which exchanges `A` with `P` and `B` with `Q`. #7051 names this profile as not settled.
2. **The sixteen census profiles still open are three orbits**, of sizes 8, 4 and 4. One argument per orbit is enough.
3. **Twelve of those sixteen are not character-excluded.** For the 8-orbit of `(2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1)` and the 4-orbit of `(0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2)` an explicit rank-one decomposition passes every additive character. The argument of #7013, #7035 and #7051 cannot be repeated there.

| Orbit | Profiles | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `O1` | `(1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)` | excluded by #6942 |
| `O2` | `(2,0,1,1)`, `(0,2,1,1)`, `(1,1,2,0)`, `(1,1,0,2)`, all `/(1,1,1)` | excluded; `(1,1,2,0)` is new here |
| `O3` | eight profiles such as `(2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1)` | open; a character-surviving decomposition exists |
| `O4` | `(0,1,1,1)` and its three images, `/(1,1,2)` | open; a character-surviving decomposition exists |
| `O5` | the same four old profiles, `/(1,1,1)` | open; every box triple is character-excluded |

The surviving decompositions are `-B + (5/2)Q + (1/4)(1,3)(1,3)^T` for `(2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1)` and `(1/2)B + (1/2)(2,1)(2,1)^T + 2Q` for `(0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2)`. On each, all eight characters of the label lattice detect at least as many calls as targets. Both fail target support, so they are not candidate words.

## Claim types

- **Proof:** the symmetry lemma and the transport lemma (`PROOF.md`, Sections 2 and 3).
- **Scoped proof, conditional:** the exclusion of `(1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1)`. It uses the exclusion theorem of open PR #7035 (the theorem of open PR #7051 gives the same conclusion through the map `P <-> Q`) and the determinant and character premises of PR #6190, Section 1. None of these is reproved or replayed here. #7035 and #7051 are open and unreviewed.
- **Finite certificate:** the two surviving decompositions with their full tables of eight characters, transported to all twelve profiles of `O3` and `O4`.
- **Bounded search, not a proof:** box counts on frames spanned by the 24 primitive directions with entries of absolute value at most 4.

This is not a complete multiplication theorem.

## Evidence and reproduction

Package `research/three-frame-profile-orbits`. CPython 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root. The interpreter used locally was `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-frame-profile-orbits
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/three-frame-profile-orbits --check-source-history
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/three-frame-profile-orbits/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/three-frame-profile-orbits/verify.py
```

Observed locally:

```text
OPEN_ORBIT_BOX (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1) triples=1936 character_excluded=1854 character_surviving=82 support_passing=8 passing_both=0
OPEN_ORBIT_BOX (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2) triples=5610 character_excluded=5225 character_surviving=385 support_passing=41 passing_both=0
OPEN_ORBIT_BOX (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,1) triples=1870 character_excluded=1870 character_surviving=0 support_passing=11 passing_both=0
PASS_THREE_FRAME_PROFILE_ORBITS group=8 compositions=35 census_orbits=5 open_profiles=16 open_orbits=3 four_call_orbits=8 new_profile_box=1914 transport_checks=11264 survivor_profiles=12 controls=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/three-frame-profile-orbits outcome=partial
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES at 633774e4d9442ccd07f9e5138991d3ebb226547c
```

Both registered commands take about four seconds each.

The verifier checks, in exact rational arithmetic:

- the eight maps fix `I`, preserve the determinant, permute the labels and the targets, and act unimodularly on `ZA + ZB + ZP`;
- exactly 8 of the 24 label permutations extend to a linear map, and they are these eight;
- residual equivariance on all 35 four-call profiles and the four three-call profiles;
- the census orbits, of sizes 1, 4, 8, 4 and 4;
- the image `A + B + 2Q` of #7035's named decomposition `2B + P + Q`, with its character that detects two calls and four targets;
- all 1914 box triples of `(1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1)` are character-excluded, directly on the new profile;
- both survivor tables, recomputed on each of the twelve profiles of `O3` and `O4`;
- 11,264 comparisons of transported character tables over every census profile and every group element;
- six failure controls.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- The exclusion of `(1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1)` is conditional on the theorem of #7035 or #7051 and on the premises of #6190, Section 1. Those proofs were not replayed.
- Sixteen census profiles stay open. `O3`, `O4` and `O5` are not settled.
- The survivors show that the character test alone does not exclude `O3` or `O4`. They do not produce a word.
- The box counts are a search on 24 lines. They do not classify all rational decompositions, and decompositions with two parallel frames are outside the box.
- Four or more added frames are not treated.
- No Lean, Docker or selected cold replay was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Is the six-call orbit `O5`, represented by `(0,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)` with `R+S+T = diag(3,2)`, character-excluded? All 1870 box triples are. A proof would close four profiles. First step: run the parity-image argument of #7035 with `3 x1^2 + 2 x2^2` in place of `3 x1^2 + x2^2`. Blocker: `diag(3,2)` has determinant 6, so the 2-adic case split has to be redone.
2. Does every decomposition of `(2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1)` fail a character or target support? In the box none of 1936 triples passes both. First step: describe the decompositions that pass every character, starting from the lattice `Z^3 + Z(1/2,1/2,1/2)` of the witness, and test the subset sums for `A+Q` on that family.
3. The same question for `(0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2)`, where 385 box triples survive the characters and none passes target support.

## Related open work

- #7035 (unpaidmoon) excludes `(2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1)`. Its theorem is the input of the transported exclusion here. Its named decomposition `2B + P + Q` is transported and checked.
- #7051 (unpaidmoon) excludes `(1,1,0,2)/(1,1,1)` and poses the question answered here. It maps to `(1,1,2,0)` under `P <-> Q`, so it gives the same conclusion independently of #7035.
- #7013 (unpaidmoon) excludes `(0,2,1,1)/(1,1,1)`, the fourth profile of the same orbit. By the transport lemma the three exclusions #7013, #7035 and #7051 are images of one another.
- #7024, #7067, #7076 and #7083 (unpaidmoon) study four, five and six added frames. They are a different equation and are not used.
- #7125, #7126 and #7127, opened from this account after the claim for this PR, study helper-462 shear words, paired-star thin rank and E8 port counts. None of them concerns the three-frame count profiles, and no number is shared.

## Credit

The register model is Cinna Davis's PR2085/2112 formal model. The determinant, support and character premises are the PR2910 package as recorded by apoursh in #6190. The census is discussion comment 19377345. The exclusions of `(1,1,1,1)`, `(0,2,1,1)`, `(2,0,1,1)` and `(1,1,0,2)` are unpaidmoon's #6942, #7013, #7035 and #7051. The symmetry lemma, the transported exclusion, the two surviving witnesses and the checker are produced by Nick Petalas.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At head `633774e4d9442ccd07f9e5138991d3ebb226547c`, [run 42906716667](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42906716667) failed in the `plan` job ([job 130146489645](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42906716667/job/130146489645)), and the package `replay` job was skipped because `plan` failed. The evidence for this PR is the local runs listed above.

The `plan` failure is one test of 760 (24 skipped) in the "Onboarding helper tests" step:

```text
FAIL: test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record (test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record)
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found in '# CI verification\n\n## Current selected-family replay: #6030 ...'
Ran 760 tests in 144.583s
FAILED (failures=1, skipped=24)
```

The cause is on `main`, not in this PR. At `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` is still headed "Current selected-family replay: #6030" and does not contain that command. This PR changes only files under `research/three-frame-profile-orbits/`.

The same single test is the only failure, with the same 760/24 counts and `replay` skipped, in five other runs from today that I read: [42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314) and [42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790) on other contributors' branches, and [42905202459](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905202459) (#7125), [42905330981](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905330981) (#7126) and [42905806694](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905806694) (#7127). No fix or retrigger was pushed, and the job was not re-run.
